channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajikistan Shares Multilingual Education Experience at Regional Forum
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Education and Science participated in a roundtable with Central Asian countries and Mongolia in Ashgabat. The discussion focused on enhancing regional cooperation through multilingual education. The minister highlighted the importance of exchanging experiences, emphasizing that linguistic diversity should improve learning quality and foster good neighborly relations. Tajikistan's language policy supports the state language while respecting others and promoting foreign language study.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prison System Withholds Karim Massimov's Personal File Details
item.description: Kazakhstan's Committee for Penal System Enforcement (KSES) has refused to disclose details about former National Security Committee head Karim Massimov's prison life. A request for information regarding his employment, salary, library use, and living conditions was denied, citing personal data protection. The KSES confirmed Massimov is serving his 18-year sentence but withheld specifics on his institution, region, work, medical visits, or family contact.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Bank Head: New Social Aid Rules Won't Affect Deposits
item.description: The head of Kazakhstan's National Bank, Timur Suleimenov, believes new requirements for social assistance, which consider deposit savings, will not significantly impact the deposit market. He stated that individuals eligible for social aid likely do not hold substantial funds in deposits, as such savings would typically preclude them from needing state assistance.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Bank Head Discusses Pension Fund Investment Strategy
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank Chairman Timur Suleimenov addressed the declining yield of pension fund assets amidst the tenge's strengthening against the dollar. He emphasized the need to invest the 28 trillion tenge of pension assets in various instruments, including foreign ones, to manage currency risks and ensure growth, rejecting the idea of simply depositing all funds due to economic limitations.

item.title: Russia Attacks Ukrainian Power Plants and Regions, Four Injured
item.description: On October 23, 2026, Russian forces attacked energy and civilian targets in Ukraine, damaging a thermal power plant and striking Sumy, Poltava, and Dnipropetrovsk regions. Four people were injured, according to Ukrainian authorities. DTEK reported its thermal power plants have been attacked over 230 times since the invasion began.

item.title: Kazakhstan Implements Key Water Sector Projects with International Bank Support
item.description: Kazakhstan is actively engaged in significant water sector projects, leveraging the support of international financial institutions. These initiatives aim to improve water management and infrastructure within the country, reflecting a commitment to sustainable development in this critical area.

item.title: Tashkent Region and Powerscape Global Sign Energy Cooperation Memorandum
item.description: The governor of Tashkent region met with Powerscape Global's founder to discuss investment cooperation, industrial projects, and modern technologies in the energy sector. Special attention was given to coal processing for electricity and fertilizer production. A memorandum of cooperation was signed.

item.title: Bishkek City Council Deputy Detained on Fraud Suspicion, Placed Under House Arrest
item.description: Taalaibek Zhakypov, a deputy of the Bishkek City Council, has been detained on suspicion of fraud. The court ordered him to be placed under house arrest until December 20. He is prohibited from leaving his residence between 10 PM and 6 AM and from leaving Bishkek without permission.

item.title: First Russian Diesel Fuel Tanker Departs for United States
item.description: The first tanker carrying Russian diesel fuel has departed for New York. The vessel, Agioi Fanendes, took on approximately 35,700 tons of diesel in the Baltic port of Primorsk and is expected to arrive in the US on November 7. This shipment follows an agreement between the US and Russian presidents regarding Russian diesel exports to global markets.

item.title: Uzbek President Orders Support for Sulton Tex Group Expansion
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has instructed the National Bank to develop a financing plan for the expansion of the Sulton Tex Group textile cluster in Kashkadarya. The company, currently employing nearly 8,000 people, aims to significantly increase job creation. The president emphasized the project's social importance and potential to become a major industrial driver for the region.

item.title: Dushanbe hosts SCO meeting on transport corridors and logistics development
item.description: The first round table on "SCO Transport and Logistics" was held in Dushanbe, focusing on expanding cooperation among Shanghai Cooperation Organisation member states. Organized by the Chamber of Commerce and Industry and the Ministry of Transport of Tajikistan, the event aimed to enhance transport and logistics sectors. Participants discussed opportunities for increased collaboration.

item.title: US Seeks to Reduce Reliance on China for Minerals, Eyes Central Asia
item.description: The United States is turning to Central Asian countries to lessen its dependence on China for critical mineral supplies, supporting mining projects in Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. However, high costs, supply chain complexities, and China's regional dominance pose significant challenges. Despite discussions, progress on China's mineral export restrictions remains elusive.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Bank head doubts new social aid rules will affect bank deposits
item.description: Timur Suleimenov, head of Kazakhstan's National Bank, believes new rules for targeted social assistance (ASP) will not lead to money withdrawal from bank deposits. He stated that most citizens rely on their own earnings and business, not social aid, and those needing support likely have minimal savings.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Bank denies artificial strengthening of the tenge
item.description: Timur Suleimenov, head of Kazakhstan's National Bank, stated that the tenge's strengthening is not artificial. He attributed it to increased export revenues from rising oil and metal prices, foreign investment in government bonds, and companies borrowing in foreign currency. The exchange rate is market-driven, he affirmed.

item.title: Kazakhstan's New Constitution Aims to Adapt Political System to Changing Realities
item.description: Abdulla Tokenov, a senior expert at the Institute of Public Policy, stated that Kazakhstan's new constitution is designed to make the country and its political system more resilient and adaptable to evolving circumstances. He emphasized the importance of this reform for long-term adaptation to new global challenges, including geopolitical, economic, and technological shifts.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Numerous Violations Found at Temporary Storage Warehouses
item.description: The General Prosecutor's Office of Kazakhstan reported systemic violations of customs legislation at temporary storage warehouses nationwide. Twenty-one warehouses had their operations suspended, and 23 administrative cases were filed against their owners. Deficiencies included missing railway tracks, inadequate fencing, and lack of surveillance cameras.

item.title: Uzbekistan National Investment Fund Completes IPO, Plans Further State Company Listings
item.description: The Uzbekistan National Investment Fund (UzNIF), managed by Franklin Templeton, conducted an IPO on London and Tashkent stock exchanges in May 2026, raising nearly $700 million for the state. The fund's portfolio includes stakes in 13 state companies. The director discussed future IPOs, dividends, and energy reforms.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China Trade Data Discrepancies Reach Record $12.7 Billion
item.description: Trade data discrepancies between Kazakhstan and China in 2024 have reached a record $12.7 billion. This figure represents the difference between official Chinese statistics and Kazakh customs data for goods crossing the border. Kazakh authorities have partially acknowledged the problem but have yet to resolve it, with President Tokayev previously linking the issue to contraband and corruption.

item.title: Head of KazMunayGas Expects Continued Cooperation with Lukoil
item.description: The head of KazMunayGas, Askhat Khasenov, stated that Lukoil, a Russian company under Western sanctions, remains a strategic partner. He indicated that issues related to attracting financing for joint ventures, whose accounts are blocked due to sanctions, are currently being addressed. KazMunayGas is actively seeking solutions to cooperation challenges with Lukoil.

item.title: Tokayev: First President Nazarbayev's Name Will Never Be Forgotten
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that the name of the First President, Nursultan Nazarbayev, who laid the foundation for independent Kazakhstan and contributed to its development, will never be forgotten. Tokayev emphasized the importance of justice in building a unified society and noted the naming of a new party 'Adilet' (Justice).

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Bank Explains Why Food Prices Aren't Falling Despite Tenge Strengthening
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank lowered the base interest rate by 0.5%, citing reduced inflation and stable domestic economic conditions. Despite the tenge strengthening against the ruble and dollar, food prices remain high due to Kazakhstan's import dependency, with imports accounting for about 28% of the food market.

item.title: Elon Musk lifts Starlink restrictions for Ukraine, says Trump
item.description: Former US President Donald Trump stated that Elon Musk has lifted Starlink internet restrictions for the Ukrainian army, restoring connectivity. This announcement followed Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's comment that Starshield, a more secure network, had not been fully restored. Trump's statement comes amid pressure on Zelensky to halt attacks on Russian oil refineries, which Trump claims are raising fuel prices.

item.title: Tajik Migrants Warned of Stricter Deportation Rules in Russia from November 2026
item.description: From November 2026, Russia will implement stricter deportation rules for foreign citizens, expanding the list of administrative offenses leading to expulsion. The number of articles in the Code of Administrative Offenses allowing deportation will increase from 22 to 45. This affects Tajik migrants, who may face deportation for offenses beyond immigration violations, including public order and social media posts.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Bank Head: Family Welfare Categories Won't Affect Loan Issuance
item.description: The head of Kazakhstan's National Bank, Timur Suleimenov, stated that family welfare categories will not impact loan and mortgage issuance. Banks utilize their own borrower assessment models, integrating various data sources including credit history, salary, and property information. These advanced digital scoring models provide a comprehensive risk profile for each applicant.

item.title: Kazakhstan Pensioners Entrust Over 200 Billion Tenge to Private Asset Managers
item.description: Kazakhstan's private asset management companies now oversee more than 200 billion tenge in pension savings. This figure has grown significantly in just over a month, with contributors entrusting over 60 billion tenge to these firms. Currently, six asset management companies operate in this sector.

item.title: Kazakh National Bank Explains Lower Returns on Pension Savings
item.description: The National Bank of Kazakhstan's pension assets yield lower returns than private investment firms. Chairman Timur Suleimenov attributed this to the large volume of funds managed, approximately 27 trillion tenge, compared to smaller private portfolios. He stated that while the pension fund did not incur losses, achieving higher returns is possible.

item.title: Kazakh President Emphasizes Sovereignty and Independence as Priceless Treasures
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that sovereignty and independence are the nation's most valuable treasures during a ceremony for Republic Day. He praised the older generation for their hard work and overcoming challenges, and noted the positive trend of youth respecting national history. He stressed strengthening statehood as a sacred duty.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev: Nazarbayev's Name Will Not Be Forgotten
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that the name of his predecessor, Nursultan Nazarbayev, will not be forgotten, citing his significant contributions to Kazakhstan's sovereignty and development. Tokayev acknowledged Nazarbayev's nearly 30-year rule and his subsequent loss of influence after the January 2022 events, while asserting that historical figures deserve fair assessment.

item.title: Suleimenov Responds to Storing All Pension Funds in Bank Deposits
item.description: National Bank Chairman Timur Suleimenov addressed concerns about the declining yield of the Unified Pension Fund (UPF) amid tenge appreciation. He dismissed the idea of placing all 28 trillion tenge in bank deposits, stating that no banks could handle such an amount and the economy wouldn't absorb it. He emphasized diversifying investments across various assets and currencies.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allocates 88 Trillion Tenge for Social Sector Development Over Seven Years
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced that 88 trillion tenge has been allocated to develop Kazakhstan's social sector in the last seven years. Since 2019, 1,259 healthcare facilities have been built, improving medical service quality, especially in rural areas. Over 1.7 million students receive free hot meals.

item.title: UN Experts Urge EU States to Avoid Deporting Afghans Amid Human Rights Concerns
item.description: UN human rights experts have warned European Union states against deporting Afghans, emphasizing the need for individual risk assessments and compliance with international law. They highlighted the dire human rights situation in Afghanistan, particularly for women, girls, minorities, and activists, citing risks of persecution and serious violations.

item.title: Kazakhstan National Bank Decreases Key Interest Rate to 15.75%
item.description: The National Bank of Kazakhstan has lowered its key interest rate from 16.25% to 15.75% annually. This decision comes amid declining inflation and expectations, aiming to maintain moderate monetary policy tightness. The bank anticipates potential inflation acceleration by year-end due to base effects but sees a low probability of further rate changes before 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Manufacturing Exports Increased by Over 45% in the Last Five Years
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that Kazakhstan's manufacturing exports have grown by over 45% in the past five years, indicating a new qualitative level of industrial development. The country has significantly developed its railway sector and automotive industry, attracting $155 billion in foreign investment over seven years.

item.title: National Bank Explains Decision Not to Lower Key Rate by Full 1%
item.description: The National Bank of Kazakhstan did not consider a 1% interest rate cut, opting instead for a 0.5% reduction. This decision was made due to slowing inflation, decreased inflation expectations, and a stable domestic economy. The move aims to maintain moderately tight monetary conditions to return inflation to the 5% target by 2028, while acknowledging elevated price pressures and pro-inflationary risks.

item.title: Tajikistan delegation attends ICAO Aviation Security Week in Astana
item.description: A delegation from Tajikistan's Civil Aviation Agency participated in the ICAO Aviation Security Week held in Astana, Kazakhstan, from October 20-22, 2026. The forum brought together aviation leaders and experts to discuss security issues and strengthen international cooperation against modern threats.

item.title: Uzbek First Lady Ziroat Mirziyoyeva Honored with WHO Director-General's Award for Child Health Advocacy
item.description: Ziroat Mirziyoyeva, Uzbekistan's First Lady and Chair of the 'Zamin' International Public Foundation, has received the prestigious WHO Director-General's Award 2026. The award recognizes her leadership in developing medical support systems for children with cancer and her global advocacy for every child's right to a healthy life.

item.title: Baloch Militant Groups Attack Gwadar Port and Pakistan-Iran Border Crossing
item.description: Forces from two Baloch armed groups have reportedly attacked the Gwadar port and a border crossing between Pakistan and Iran. Details regarding casualties or the extent of the damage are not yet available. This incident marks a significant escalation of activity in the region.

item.title: Complaints Rise in Uzbekistan Over Forced Bundling of Medicines
item.description: Complaints regarding the forced bundling of medicines are increasing in Uzbekistan. Some importers and wholesale distributors reportedly require the purchase of other drugs along with high-demand medications. Financial sanctions may be imposed for violations.

item.title: inDrive, Pony.ai, and NVIDIA to Pilot Self-Driving Taxis in Kazakhstan
item.description: International ride-hailing service inDrive, China's Pony.ai, and US-based NVIDIA have agreed to collaborate on launching self-driving taxis in Kazakhstan, with Astana being the potential first test city. The partnership involves assessing technical, commercial, and legal conditions for autonomous vehicles, with inDrive managing operations and NVIDIA providing tech support. Initial tests are planned for early 2027.

item.title: Barqi Tojik's debt to Rogun HPP approaches one billion somoni again
item.description: The debt of "Barqi Tojik" to the Rogun HPP is once again approaching one billion somoni. At the beginning of the year, the debt exceeded 1 billion somoni, decreased in summer, but rose again in September.
